Follow this format for e-mail signatures to keep VCH's brand cohesive.

You may download the e-mail signature template at brand.vch.ca

<visual_element id="e1">
Example e-mail signature block inside a bordered box:
- Firstname Lastname
- Job Title
- Vancouver Coastal Health
- mobile 604 123 4567
- office 604 123 4567
- e-mail firstname.lastname@vch.ca
- Grey acknowledgement text: “I acknowledge that my place of work lies on the unceded traditional homelands of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. The content of this e-mail is confidential and may be privileged. If you receive this e-mail in error, please contact the sender and delete it immediately.”
</visual_element>

<visual_element id="e2">
Annotated formatting guide showing the same signature layout with callouts:
- Name is set in black bolded Calibri at the font size 11.5.
- The job title is set in black regular Calibri at the font size 9.5.
- Vancouver Coastal Health is set in blue (RGB 0, 120, 174) bolded Calibri at the font size 9.5.
- Mobile, office and e-mail colour is blue (RGB 0, 120, 174). Contact info is black. All set in regular Calibri at the font size 9.5.
- The First Nations acknowledgement and confidentiality statement are grey (RGB 113, 113, 113) regular Calibri at the font size 7.5.
- “1 space here at the font size 5” appears twice beside dashed spacing lines.
- The signature example repeats: Firstname Lastname; Job Title; Vancouver Coastal Health; mobile 604 123 4567; office 604 123 4567; e-mail firstname.lastname@vch.ca; grey acknowledgement/confidentiality text.
</visual_element>

Note:
- Please change the First Nations listed in the acknowledgement to align with your specific location. The First Nation Recognition Protocols document lists the First Nations of each community.
- Do not add your own images, logos, background patterns, quotes, links or extra text to the signature.

#### 2026 General Local Election Candidate Information

General Local Elections are held every four years for Mayor and Council.  Candidates are voted in for a four-year term.  Electors in McBride vote to choose:

  * One (1) Mayor
  * Four (4) Councillors

#### Candidate Resources:

If you are planning or thinking about seeking election in the 2026 General Local Election please visit Elections BC for the most up to date resources and legislation regarding Campaign Advertising and Financing.  

  * Candidate's Guide to Local Elections in B.C. 2026
  * 2026 Handbook for Local Candidates
  * 2026 Guide to Campaign Financing for Local Candidates and Financial Agents in B.C.
  * Online Learning

All other inquiries regarding the 2026 General Local Election can be directed to the following:

Sherri Flynn, Chief Election Officer:
Phone: 250-569-2229
Email: sherri@mcbride.ca
Amanda Moore, Deputy Chief Election Officer:
Phone: 250-569-2229
Email: amanda@mcbride.ca

#### Who Can Run for Council

A person is qualified to be nominated, elected and to hold office as a member of Local Government if they meet the following criteria;

  * Canadian citizen;
  * 18 years of age or older on General Voting Day: October 17, 2026;
  * resident of British Columbia for at least 6 months immediately before the day nomination papers are filed; and
  * are not disqualified by the Local Government Act or any other enactment from being nominated for, being elected to, or holding office, or be otherwise disqualified by law.
  * a Social Insurance Card issued by Human Resources Development Canada;
  * a Citizenship Card issued by Citizenship and Immigration Canada;
  * a Document, issued by the Government of Canada, that certifies that the applicant is registered as an Indian under the Indian Act (Canada), such as a status card;
  * a Citizenship or membership card issued by a First Nation;
  * a Citizenship card issued by Métis Nation British Columbia;
  * a real property tax notice issued under section 237 of the Community Charter;
  * a credit card or debit card issued by a savings institution as defined in section 29 of the Interpretation Act;
  * a utility bill issued for the supply of electricity, natural gas, water, telephone services or coaxial cable services;
  * a Birth certificate; or
  * Canadian passport

The only electors who may vote are electors who are qualified under the Local Government Act and who, on the date on which the special voting opportunity is held, and before the end of the voting hours for the special voting opportunity, have been admitted as patients to the McBride & District Hospital or as residents of the Beaver View Lodge in McBride.

# Multi-Source Feedback

​​​Benefits of participating in MSF:

  * Medical staff can review report results with a trained reviewer from their department in a 1:1 conversation.
  * Medical leaders can develop coaching skills to support facilitated feedback conversations in their departments.
  * Medical staff are eligible to receive CPD credits for participating in the MSF process.
  * ​For more information, please view the Multi-Source Feedback infographic, MSF Process, MSF Participant Overview, and MSF Evaluator Overview

## Coaching Tools and Resources:

  * Read the Facilitated Reflective Performance Feedback article paper for background info.
  * See the R2C2 Handout guide to support coaching conservations.
  * Watch a refresher video of a coaching conversation using the R2C2 model.
  * Visiting the Medical Staff Leadership Development Resources for additional coaching tools and resources​.
  * An overview of the MSF Role of Reviewer and MSF Reviewer FAQ​
 ​​FAQ:

  1. How do I participate?
     * ​​​​​Contact the Medical, Quality, Leadership and Practice Team at medicalquality@vch.ca. 
  2. Will my MSF report be shared with anyone other than me?
     * ​​​​No, this report is confidential and only accessible to you; it is not associated with credentialing and privileging and you get to choose who you share the results with. 
  3. What departments have MSF available?
     * ​​​​MSF is available to all departments.
